writeup.headline: Sandisk rates Buy on explosive growth and net cash, held back by high absolute valuation.
writeup.thesis: Sandisk scores 67, a Buy, just 3 points above the Hold line. Growth scores 100 on TTM revenue growth of 175.3% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 371.6% year on year, with growth having sped up by 120.6 pp from the previous quarter. The balance sheet also scores 100 thanks to net cash and no debt. Quality is solid at 74, with a 71.5% gross margin and 61.2% operating margin, but this is scored on a normalised FCF margin of 10.8% rather than the reported 56.8%, and the diluted share count is up 6.9% year on year. Valuation scores only 22: in absolute terms P/S of 10.2x and P/FCF of 94.3x on normalised FCF are high, with the FCF yield 3.9 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, and there is no comparison with its own history.
key_risks: Memory pricing is cyclical; the surge in revenue and margins could reverse if NAND prices fall.
High absolute valuation leaves little cushion if results or guidance disappoint.
Shares are volatile: price 39.8% below its 52-week high and 10.6% below its 50-day average.
Q1 FY27 results are due after the close today, against an outlook of $10.30–10.80B revenue and $44–46 non-GAAP EPS.
Diluted share count up 6.9% year on year dilutes existing holders.
what_would_change: A drop of 3 points, for example from weaker trend or a negative news or guidance shift around today's results, would move the rating to Hold.
Rising 13 points to Strong Buy would likely need a better valuation score, such as normalised FCF catching up with reported FCF.
A slowdown in revenue growth would pull the growth score down from 100 and could tip the rating to Hold.
